stem: Harry is a 2-year-old boy with a barking cough and stridor at rest, with a clear chest and recent coryzal symptoms. Which one of the following is the most likely organism?
explanation: This is classic viral croup (laryngotracheitis), most commonly caused by parainfluenza virus. The barking cough, inspiratory stridor, and mild preceding URTI symptoms in a previously well child are typical.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Emergency Medicine - Breathing difficulties

rationale: The stem describes classic croup, whose most common pathogen is parainfluenza virus.

optionExplanations.A: Correct — parainfluenza virus is the most common cause of croup.
optionExplanations.B: Can cause bacterial tracheitis, but the presentation here is more consistent with viral croup.
optionExplanations.C: Can cause epiglottitis, but immunisations are up to date and the presentation is not typical.
optionExplanations.D: Can cause severe pharyngitis or invasive infection, but not the classic croup picture.
optionExplanations.E: Causes diphtheria, which is rare in immunised children and usually presents differently.

Clinical scenario 3 - Harry

Harry, a two year old boy, presents with a barking cough and stridor at rest. He had been well up until this evening, apart from a mild runny nose and slight cough. On examination he has moderate respiratory distress with intercostal and subcostal recessions and tug. His RR is 35, HR 140 and saturations 94% in room air. He has a clear chest and inspiratory stridor at rest. He has been previously well and his immunisations are up to date.

The following five questions refer to Harry's clinical scenario.
